title: How Your Morning Mood May Affect Your Workday
paragraphs: The alarm goes off, and it's time to get up for work. On some mornings, we're ready to start the day. On others, we just want to turn off the alarm and go back to sleep.
But could the way we feel about the day ahead affect how well we focus at work? Well, a new study suggests that it could.
Researchers from Canada and Germany studied 102 people over two working weeks. The participants answered questions three times a day, sharing how they felt before, during and after their working day.
The researchers wanted to understand something called "flow." This is when we're so focused on what we're doing that we forget about everything else — and work very well.
They found that people who looked forward to their day were more likely to experience flow.
People who expected to learn new things or face challenges also seemed a little more likely to experience flow, but the results were less clear.
Those who were worried that the day would be difficult or stressful were less likely to experience flow.
The researchers also looked at sleep. They found that people who slept better were more likely to look forward to the day ahead and less likely to worry about it.
And there was another interesting finding — people who experienced more flow during the day were less likely to lie in bed at night thinking about problems from their jobs.
The researchers said employers can help by giving their staff clear goals and time to focus without interruptions.
Of course, the study doesn't prove that positive thoughts lead to better days at work. But it does suggest that the way we think about the day ahead may make a difference to how well we focus!
